First day of the observed weather the reach is driven over, 'YYYY-MM-DD' - from phrasing like 'last week' or 'the first week of August'. The station record is hourly and the network holds the last two weeks, so an earlier day refuses typed [supplied on this invocation]

Last day of the observed weather, 'YYYY-MM-DD'. The run is sim_duration_s long from the first observation, so this day has to be far enough past weather_start to cover it; at most 14 days after [supplied on this invocation]

Where the temperature series and its diurnal range are read, as a Point: the pick's {coordinates, name} verbatim, a (lon, lat) pair, 'lat,lon', a point layer, or a place name [supplied on this invocation]
Result-writing cadence; unset keeps the steering file's own period [supplied on this invocation]
Modelled reach length downstream of the geocoded point; the water warms with the time it spends in the reach, so the length is how much exposure the question asks about [supplied on this invocation]

Simulated time. A DIURNAL RANGE needs whole days, and this defaults to seven; a shorter run answers what the reach did over that window and no more. The weather record has to span every second of it - a run longer than its own forcing refuses rather than extrapolating [supplied on this invocation; CLAMPED from 1800 to the declared minimum 3600 s]
Target element edge length the reach is triangulated at; a surface heat budget is a reach-scale answer, so this is coarser than a plume question asks for [supplied on this invocation]
